translation_en: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Yahya, from ‘Ubayd ibn Hunayn, who heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrate: He said: For a year I wanted to ask ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not ask him out of awe of him. Then he went out for Hajj, and I went with him. On our return, when we were on part of the road, he turned aside to the arak trees to attend to a need. I waited for him until he had finished, then walked with him and said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, who were the two wives who supported one another against the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him?’ He said, ‘Hafsah and ‘A’ishah.’ I said, ‘By Allah, I have wanted to ask you about this for a year, but I could not, out of awe of you.’ He said, ‘Do not do that. Whatever you think I know, ask me about it. If I know it, I will tell you.’ ‘Umar then said, ‘By Allah, in the pre-Islamic period we did not consider women to have any standing, until Allah revealed what He revealed about them and assigned them what He assigned them.’ He continued: While I was considering a matter, my wife said, ‘If you did such-and-such…’ I said to her, ‘What is the matter with you? Why are you involving yourself in something I intend to do?’ She said, ‘How strange you are, Ibn al-Khattab! You do not want anyone to answer you back, yet your daughter answers the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, until he remains angry for the whole day.’ ‘Umar got up, took his cloak, and went straight to Hafsah. He said to her, ‘My daughter, you answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, until he remains angry for the whole day?’ Hafsah said, ‘By Allah, we do answer him back.’ I said, ‘You know that I am warning you of Allah’s punishment and the anger of His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. My daughter, do not be deceived by the love of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, for this woman whose beauty amazes her’—meaning ‘A’ishah. Then I left and went to Umm Salamah, because of my kinship with her, and spoke to her. Umm Salamah said, ‘How strange you are, Ibn al-Khattab! You have involved yourself in everything, to the point that you want to intrude between the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and his wives.’ By Allah, she rebuked me so firmly that it restrained some of what I had been feeling. I left her. I had an Ansari companion: when I was away, he would bring me the news, and when he was away, I would bring him the news. We were afraid of one of the kings of Ghassan, for we had been told that he intended to march against us, and our hearts were filled with fear of him. Then my Ansari companion knocked at the door and said, ‘Open, open!’ I said, ‘Has the Ghassani come?’ He said, ‘Something more serious than that: the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has separated himself from his wives.’ I said, ‘May Hafsah and ‘A’ishah be humiliated!’ I took my garment and went out. I found the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in an upper room that he climbed to by a ladder. A black servant of the Messenger of Allah was at the top of the stairs. I said to him, ‘Tell him that this is ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.’ He gave me permission. ‘Umar said: I told the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, this whole account. When I reached the part about Umm Salamah, the Messenger of Allah smiled. He was lying on a mat with nothing between him and it, and beneath his head was a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber. Near his feet was some acacia fruit poured out, and near his head were some hides hanging up. I saw the marks of the mat on his side, and I wept. He said, ‘Why are you weeping?’ I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Chosroes and Caesar have all that they have, while you are the Messenger of Allah.’ He said, ‘Are you not content that they have this world and we have the Hereafter?’
